name: Auxiliares Sagittarii Lecti

abilities.name: Rapid Advance
abilities.text: Improved unit movement speed over an extended period.

abilities.name: Barrage
abilities.text: Loose projectiles more frequently for an extended period of time.

abilities.name: Precision Shot
abilities.text: Improved missile weapon damage for an extended period. These values are further modified by the unit itself.

abilities.name: Shield Wall
abilities.text: The unit moves into a close formation and raises shields.

attributes.name: Resistant to Fatigue
attributes.text: Fatigue has less of an effect on this unit.

attributes.name: Hide (forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in forests until enemy units get too close.

short: The name sagittarii most likely indicates that this unit was armed with bows; the word lecti means «chosen, selected, excellent», implying that they were not ordinary archers, but skilled and chosen ones. Auxilia (latin) - an auxiliary unit of the Roman army.  There is a strong opinion that auxilia units consisted of barbarians-volunteers (primarily Germanic). Vegetius directly mentions that the legions were composed of Roman citizens, and the auxilia of barbarians. About the internal organisation of the auxilia nothing is definitely known, but most likely, the structure of these units in the 4th century was no different from the legions. While the legions were composed of forcefully conscripted Romanised barbarians who lived on the territory of the Empire, in the auxilia served mainly volunteers from the Germanic tribes beyond the Rhine. Such system led to the fact that the auxiliaries became superior to the legionnaires in terms of their combat qualities.
history: In the face of an increasing number of barbarian incursions, the effective defence of Rome’s now-sprawling territory became a serious problem in the 4th century AD. The Emperor Constantine’s controversial solution was to divide the army into two halves. 'Limitanei', literally ‘the men on the limes’ or 'borders', were frontier garrison troops intended to pin down an invading force until the full-time 'comitatenses', the late-Roman equivalent of the traditional Legionaries, could arrive to deal with the situation decisively. Although well-equipped, limitanei were generally considered by all to be second-class warriors. This was possibly because they were often part-time soldiers who had been encouraged to settle and farm the land around their outposts in exchange for policing the Empire's borders.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
